recorded: Every case passed against the original with Node.js 26.12.1, tsx 4.23.1, @langchain/core 0.3.80, @langchain/langgraph 0.2.74, and @langchain/openai 0.3.17, run as "node --import tsx src/{program}.ts". The original always calls OpenRouter's address, so the copy that produced these cases reads OPENAI_BASE_URL first and falls back to that address, a one-line change in the model factory. No OpenRouter key was available, so the model answers were recorded from Ollama 0.40.11 through its OpenAI-compatible API, with gemma4:12b-mlx standing in for openai/gpt-4o-mini and without the stand-in's reasoning field, while the requests keep the model the program asked for. The provider failure replays OpenRouter's documented error for a missing key. Incident ids are random and feed back into the conversation, so the output accepts any id, tool results that carry one are checked by their call id only, and no case resolves an incident it has just opened. Latencies may be any number of milliseconds. The messages about a missing key are checked by their first sentence, because the rest suggests Node.js commands.
